- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.2) — model tends to overshoot after bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (especially < -0.1) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after recent spikes, especially if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to over- or under-forecasting in the following 3–5 days.
- Overshoot after spikes: if price spikes >+5% from recent high, model often forecasts higher than true outcome, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating volatility in early days of the forecast window, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Sentiment-driven drift: if sentiment turns positive mid-forecast, model often fails to adjust downward in the final 5–7 days — true price tends to stabilize or dip.
